novel_features.name: SNAP Signature Debugger
novel_features.description: Build and inspect both SNAP signatures locally — see the exact string-to-sign, body hash, and headers so a 403 is diagnosed in seconds instead of bisected by hand.
novel_features.rationale: Constructs the full RSA-SHA256 + HMAC-SHA512 signing pipeline locally; today this exists only inside Postman pre-request scripts.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever a SNAP call returns 401/403 — it shows every signing intermediate without touching the API.

novel_features.name: SNAP Token Lifecycle & Keygen
novel_features.description: Check cached B2B token freshness against the 900-second TTL, and generate the RSA-2048 keypair SNAP onboarding requires with 'snap keygen'.
novel_features.rationale: Folds the openssl-dictated-over-a-call onboarding step and token babysitting into the CLI's credential store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use during SNAP onboarding or whenever token expiry is a suspected 401 cause.

novel_features.name: Smart Payment Routing
novel_features.description: Charge a payment with the right API surface chosen automatically — SNAP where the method supports it, legacy otherwise, with --surface to override.
novel_features.rationale: Requires both the legacy Basic client and the hand-built SNAP signing client in one binary plus a method-to-surface policy table.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this over raw charge/snap commands when you want company-policy-correct surface selection per payment method.

novel_features.name: Smart Payout Routing
novel_features.description: Send a disbursement via SNAP transfer-interbank or e-wallet topup with account inquiry first, falling back to legacy batch submit when asked.
novel_features.rationale: Routes across both API surfaces and sequences inquiry-then-transfer, which no single endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for one-off pay-outs from the terminal; use 'disbursements' commands for legacy batch flows.

novel_features.name: SNAP Response-Code Explainer
novel_features.description: Decode any SNAP response code offline — meaning, originating service, HTTP status, and the likely fix.
novel_features.rationale: Seeds the 48-row SNAP response-code catalog from the docs into local SQLite; no doc-tab hunting.
novel_features.why_it_matters: First stop when a SNAP call returns a non-2xx responseCode.

novel_features.name: Sandbox Simulation Helper
novel_features.description: Print the exact sandbox magic values (even/odd account numbers, magic amounts) that force a success, pending, or failure outcome.
novel_features.rationale: The simulation rules live scattered across two docs pages; the CLI seeds them as a queryable table.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when writing integration tests against the sandbox to force specific outcomes deterministically.

novel_features.name: Order/Payment Reconciliation
novel_features.description: Join synced orders against payments locally to flag charged-but-unsettled orders, payments with no order, and amount mismatches.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-entity SQLite join over synced data; no Durianpay endpoint answers this in one call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run at period close instead of exporting two CSVs and VLOOKUPing them.

novel_features.name: Refund Audit
novel_features.description: Flag refunds that exceed their source payment, target unsettled payments, or duplicate an earlier refund.
novel_features.rationale: Joins refunds against payments in the local store — a query shape the API cannot express.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use during reconciliation to catch refund anomalies before finance does.

novel_features.name: Stuck-Disbursement Detector
novel_features.description: List disbursements still pending past a chosen age, bucketed against Durianpay's 2/5/10/90/210-minute webhook retry ladder.
novel_features.rationale: Time-windowed query over synced disbursements with the retry ladder seeded as context.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as the disbursement-ops health check — anything bucketed past the final retry needs manual chase.

novel_features.name: Completion-Signature Verifier
novel_features.description: Recompute the HMAC-SHA256(disbursement_id|amount) completion signature locally and compare it to the webhook's value.
novel_features.rationale: The scheme is documented only inside an integration guide; the CLI makes it a one-liner.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when validating a disbursement-completion callback before marking a payout settled.

narrative.headline: Every Durianpay API in one terminal — legacy and SNAP — with the dual-signature scheme handled for you and a local SQLite store no SDK has.
narrative.value_prop: Durianpay has no CLI, no MCP server, and no maintained SDK; SNAP signing exists only inside Postman pre-request scripts. This CLI wraps both API generations, mints and caches B2B tokens, signs every SNAP request (RSA-SHA256 + HMAC-SHA512) transparently, and routes payments to the right surface per method. Synced orders, payments, refunds, and disbursements land in SQLite for reconciliation joins the API can't express.
narrative.auth_narrative: Two credential sets. Legacy: set DURIANPAY_API_KEY (sandbox keys start dp_test_, live dp_live_) — sent as HTTP Basic with the key as username. SNAP additionally needs DURIANPAY_SNAP_CLIENT_KEY, DURIANPAY_SNAP_CLIENT_SECRET, DURIANPAY_SNAP_PRIVATE_KEY (path to your RSA-2048 private key PEM), DURIANPAY_SNAP_CHANNEL_ID, and optionally DURIANPAY_SNAP_PARTNER_ID (defaults to the client key); generate the keypair with 'snap keygen' and upload the public key in Dashboard > Settings > API Keys. Sandbox and live credentials are completely separate — switch with 'durianpay-pp-cli env sandbox' / 'env live'.

quickstart.comment: Verify config, credentials, and API reachability before anything else
Decode a SNAP response code offline — works with zero credentials
First authenticated call: list recent orders (legacy surface)
Pull recent activity into the local SQLite store
Join orders against payments locally to surface settlement gaps

troubleshoots.fix: Check DURIANPAY_API_KEY is set and matches the environment — sandbox keys (dp_test_) fail against live; run 'doctor' to see which env is active

Run 'snap sign --method POST --path <path> --body @req.json --debug' to inspect the string-to-sign and both signatures; commonest causes are an unminified body hash, expired B2B token (900s TTL), or the public key not uploaded to the dashboard
Confirm DURIANPAY_SNAP_PRIVATE_KEY points at the RSA private key whose public half is uploaded in Dashboard > Settings > API Keys for the SAME environment

troubleshoots.symptom: Duplicate X-EXTERNAL-ID error on SNAP transactions
troubleshoots.fix: X-EXTERNAL-ID must be unique per calendar day; the CLI auto-generates one — pass --external-id only when you intend an idempotent retry of the same logical request
These read the local store — run 'sync --resources orders,payments,refunds,disbursements --since 30d' first

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for Durianpay payment and disbursement operations from the terminal or from AI agents: charging payments, sending pay-outs, checking statuses, minting SNAP tokens, debugging SNAP signatures, simulating sandbox outcomes, and running reconciliation joins over synced local data. It is the right choice whenever a task names Durianpay, SNAP signatures for Durianpay, or Indonesian payment/disbursement ops against api.durianpay.id.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for other Indonesian gateways (Xendit, Midtrans, Doku) — the SNAP signing here is wired to Durianpay's endpoints and credential model
Do not use it to build checkout UIs — that's the Durianpay web/mobile SDKs' job; this CLI is server-side API operations only
Do not use it for Durianpay dashboard administration (user management, settlement schedule changes) — those have no public API
Do not point it at production with --env live for testing — sandbox credentials and 'sandbox simulate' exist for that

recipes.title: Debug a SNAP 403 in one command
recipes.explanation: Prints the minified body, its SHA-256 hex, the full string-to-sign, and the resulting X-SIGNATURE so you can see exactly which input diverges.

recipes.title: Send a payout with account verification
recipes.explanation: Runs SNAP account inquiry first, then transfer-interbank, with the B2B token minted/cached automatically.

recipes.title: Period-close reconciliation
recipes.explanation: Syncs a month of activity then joins orders against payments locally, flagging unsettled and mismatched rows.

recipes.title: Narrow a deep payment object for an agent
recipes.explanation: Payment objects are verbose; --select with dotted paths keeps agent context small.

recipes.title: Force a sandbox failure case
recipes.explanation: Prints the odd-numbered account value that makes the sandbox reject the transfer, ready to paste into a test.
